idempotency.verified_at: The "Idempotency/Upsert Behavior" section of https://api.noru.tech/llms.txt states that for `POST /v1/privacy/datamaps` and the ingestDatamap MCP tool, the write is keyed on `slug` within the organization: identical content is a no-op, and a changed manifest is upserted — each system, dataset and processing activity it names is created or updated in place on its `fides_key`, and anything the manifest no longer names is soft-archived rather than deleted, so a push replaces the data map for that slug rather than merging into it. The endpoint's own description repeats it, and so does the ingestDatamap tool description published by https://api.noru.tech/v1/mcp. The same section records that the content checksum excludes `commitSha` and `branch`, which is what makes re-pushing unchanged content from a new commit a no-op rather than a re-materialization.

source.note: The schemas, models, migrations and API contracts the repository actually contains. This half of the queue is repo-resident truth: no server-side integration can see which columns exist on a branch that has not merged, and no API key can read a migration.

outputs.purpose: The data map in Ethyca's own on-disk format, for the `fides` CLI and anything else that reads a Fides manifest. It is not the manifest: `.noru/privacy-datamap.yml` carries the citations, the attribution and the review state, and is what `:push` is bound to; this is that content projected down to plain Fideslang with the piece's own bookkeeping removed. Keeping the conventional path is the whole point — a data map the ecosystem's tooling cannot read is a data map that only Noru can use.
